name: Alger Centre
tagline: White colonial arcades above the bay
description: The downtown core of Haussmann-style white facades, arched seafront arcades and stepped streets running up from the port, centred on Rue Didouche Mourad. Cafes, bookshops and ministries fill it. Everything from the Casbah to the Grande Poste is walkable, and old high-ceilinged flats rent cheaply.
bestFor: Nomads who want to walk to cafes, the sea and the old city without ever needing a car
pros: Best walkability in the city with metro and tram links
Beautiful old apartments with balconies and sea views
Cafes, markets and street food on every block
cons: Traffic noise and near impossible parking
Buildings are old with weak plumbing and slow internet
Streets get sketchy in the lower quarters after dark

name: Hydra
description: A hillside district of villas, gated residences and embassy compounds above the centre, with the Sidi Yahia strip of boutiques, patisseries and restaurants at its heart. Diplomats and Algerian professionals live here. Rents are the highest in the country but power, internet and security are the most dependable.
bestFor: Remote workers on a company budget who want reliable internet and a secure building
pros: Most reliable internet and utilities in Algiers
Sidi Yahia restaurants, gyms and supermarkets close by
Quiet, green and safe to walk in the evening
cons: By far the priciest rents in the city
Steep hills and heavy traffic funnelling down to the centre
Feels sealed off from ordinary Algerian life

name: El Biar
tagline: Hilltop residential quarter with real neighbourhood life
description: A breezy plateau above Hydra with a proper high street of bakeries, greengrocers and old cafes, plus tree-shaded residential streets of 1950s blocks. Families and academics dominate. It gives you a genuine local neighbourhood and cooler summer air, with the centre a short taxi or bus ride down.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads wanting a normal neighbourhood at less than Hydra prices
pros: Real high street with markets, bakeries and cafes
Cooler and quieter than the seafront in summer
Cheaper than neighbouring Hydra for similar quality
cons: Steep streets and a slow commute down to the centre
Very few English speakers, French or Arabic needed

name: Kouba
tagline: Middle-class hillside with newer apartment blocks
description: A large hillside district southeast of the centre, mixing older houses around the historic mosque with newer residential complexes and busy shopping streets. It is solidly middle class and well served by buses and the metro extension. Modern flats cost far less here than anywhere on the embassy hill.
bestFor: Nomads on a normal budget who want a modern flat and can accept a commute
pros: Metro and bus links into the centre
Plenty of everyday shops and cheap eating
cons: Bland residential feel with little atmosphere
Congested main roads at peak hours
Nothing aimed at foreigners or coworking

name: Bab Ezzouar
tagline: Student and business zone near the airport
description: A modern eastern satellite built around the USTHB university campus, with tower blocks, an office park and one of the country's biggest shopping malls. Students and corporate staff fill it. Rents are low, the airport is ten minutes away and the coastal motorway and metro run straight to the centre.
bestFor: Budget nomads and frequent flyers who want low rent and quick airport access
pros: Cheap rents and cheap student eating
Ten minutes from the airport, metro to the centre
Modern buildings with better plumbing than downtown
cons: Charmless concrete sprawl with no old-city character
Around 13km out, so downtown trips take time
Dead and echoing outside university term
